Please describe the problem (when it happened, what you did, and what you saw).

Volume button rotation only receives volume key presses. Lab\'s status bar tap receives touches through a thin area over the status bar. It checks the scroll area only when scrolling to the top, and while the status bar is hidden it only checks whether the tapped spot is a text field. It never reads text on the screen.
Reapplies your DPI after a reboot.
Tells the system what the service above does.
Readjusts DPI when you fold or unfold. Also keeps the notification scaling controls and shake detection running when they\'re on.
Granted once via Shizuku or PC
Granted by GOAT with system settings permission
Installs new versions through the system installer when Shizuku isn\'t available. You need to turn on \'Allow app installs from GOAT\' the first time.
Used only to check for updates. New versions are downloaded from GitHub, and no other data is sent.
Shows notifications for DPI changes made elsewhere, fold/unfold detection, per-app scaling, and shake to rotate.
Used to show the margin buttons for hiding the status bar and Lab\'s app width narrowing. Granted automatically when Shizuku is connected.

Used to change screen DPI, animation speed, screen rotation, radios kept on in airplane mode, and status bar icons, and to turn on volume button rotation. Can\'t be granted through the normal permission dialog.
Used to get system settings permission without a PC and to change per-app scaling. Allow it in the Shizuku dialog.
Sorts the per-app scaling list by recent use. Granted automatically when Shizuku is connected.
Vibrates briefly when shake to rotate rotates the screen.
Keeps the device from sleeping until the background DPI check finishes.

GOAT gets system access through the free app Shizuku. Follow the steps below once to set it up.
Run the command below once in PowerShell opened from the platform-tools folder on your PC to start the GOAT shell helper. It stops when you close GOAT or don\'t use it for %1$d min.
The PC shell helper stops when you close GOAT or don\'t use it for %1$d min.
Shizuku access granted. Close this window to continue.

Per-app scale is a single DPI value, so the same value applies to both the cover and main screens. The two screens have different PPI, so the same value looks different in size. \'%1$s\' matches the device-wide scale for each screen, but per-app scale can\'t be set per screen. Choose based on the screen you use most.
Why sizes look different when folded

Turn on \'%1$s\' to show the current app and its scale in a notification. Use [Smaller], [Default], and [Larger] to change it one step at a time. Changing the scale restarts the app, and GOAT reopens it.

• App scales you've already set: kept after reboot.
• Changing scale from the list, and notification [Smaller]/[Default]/[Larger]: only while Shizuku is running.
• Current app in the notification: only updates while Shizuku is running.
• '%1$s': once permission is granted through Shizuku, it works without Shizuku.
• Wireless debugging is only needed to start Shizuku. Turn on '%2$s' and GOAT turns off wireless debugging right after Shizuku starts. Turn this option off on devices where turning off wireless debugging stops Shizuku.
Tap an app and choose \'Default\' to reset just that app, or tap ⋮ → Reset to restore all apps to the default scale. You can also reset them in Samsung\'s \'App screen size\' settings.

This setting can only be changed with system-level permission. The free app Shizuku provides it through wireless debugging. Pairing is only needed once. On Android 13 and later, Shizuku turns back on when you connect to Wi-Fi after a reboot. Instead of Shizuku, you can also start the GOAT shell helper with a single PC command.
Samsung\'s system only allows six values (%1$s), so you can\'t adjust in steps of 1. \'Default\' clears the per-app setting and follows the device-wide scale.
Why there are six scale steps
Sets a separate scale for each app. It\'s the same setting as Samsung\'s \'Settings → Display → App screen size\', so changes show there too. Values stay after a reboot.
Open an app to change its scale here

After: both screens look the same size
The main screen DPI is calculated from both screens\' resolution and PPI so they look the same size. It\'s reapplied after a reboot.
2. Set only the cover screen DPI
The two screens have different PPI (pixels per inch), so the same DPI looks different in actual size.
1. Why the same DPI looks different
The %1$s app needs the WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS permission to change screen DPI.

GOAT gets the permission after the last step. You can turn off Shizuku after that.
Tap the item that matches the error on your PC.
Install it with your distribution\'s package. On Fedora, run sudo dnf install android-tools; on Arch, run sudo pacman -S android-tools.
\nIf adb devices shows \'no permissions\', on Ubuntu/Debian run sudo apt install android-sdk-platform-tools-common, then reconnect the cable.
\nIf your distribution\'s adb is older than 30, download \'SDK Platform-Tools for Linux\' from developer.android.com and run it as ./adb.
If you have Homebrew, install it with the command below. Otherwise, download \'SDK Platform-Tools for Mac\' from the site above, unzip it, and run ./adb instead of adb from that folder.
\nWireless pairing (adb pair) requires adb 30 or later. Check with adb version.

① Download \'SDK Platform-Tools for Windows\' from developer.android.com/tools/releases/platform-tools and unzip it.\n② Shift+right-click an empty spot in the platform-tools folder and choose \'Open PowerShell window here\' or \'Open in Terminal\'.\n③ Run the commands in the steps below in this window as .\\adb.
\nIf your phone isn\'t recognized, install Samsung\'s \'Android USB Driver for Windows\'.
A lower DPI makes text and icons smaller so more fits on screen. You can pick values in steps of 1, including ones not in Settings\' \'Screen zoom\', and they\'re reapplied after a reboot.
Connect using the \'IP address & Port\' on the main wireless debugging screen (different from the pairing port). \'connected to …\' means it worked.
GOAT checks the permission automatically when you return. Once confirmed, you can turn off %1$s.
Run the command below. If it finishes with no output, it worked.

Phone: On the wireless debugging screen, tap \'Pair device with pairing code\'. Note the IP address:port and 6-digit code shown. Keep this window open until pairing is done.\nPC: Replace the IP:port in the command below and run it, then enter the 6-digit code when asked. \'Successfully paired\' means it worked.
① Go to Settings → About phone → Software information and tap Build number 7 times to turn on Developer options.\n② Turn on Developer options → USB debugging.\n③ Connect to your PC with a USB cable.

① Go to Settings → About phone → Software information and tap Build number 7 times to turn on Developer options.\n② Connect your phone and PC to the same Wi-Fi.\n③ Turn on Developer options → Wireless debugging.
Run the command below. If your phone shows \'Allow USB debugging?\', tap [Allow]. You\'re ready when your device is listed as device.
The same phone was detected twice (for wireless, the pairing and connect connections, or USB and wireless). Pick one entry whose status is device and put its name after -s.
When it says more than one device
If you haven\'t installed it, install it with the steps above. If you\'re using the zip file, run ./adb from that folder.
In PowerShell opened from the platform-tools folder, add .\\ before adb.
Make sure it\'s a data cable, not charge-only, and that USB debugging is on.
When the device doesn\'t show up
\u0020On Windows, you may need the Samsung USB driver.
Wireless pairing requires adb version 30 or later. Also check whether an older adb bundled with another program (such as Smart Switch) is running first.

Use the IP:port from the \'Pair device with pairing code\' popup for adb pair, and the \'IP address & Port\' from the main wireless debugging screen for adb connect. The two ports are different and change when you turn wireless debugging off and on.
When the port numbers get mixed up
Tap [Allow] on the \'Allow USB debugging?\' prompt on your phone. If you don\'t see it, go to Developer options → \'Revoke USB debugging authorizations\', then reconnect the cable.

① Turn off VPN on your phone. With VPN on, devices can't find each other even on the same Wi-Fi.
② Make sure your phone and PC are on the same Wi-Fi.
③ Restart adb. If it still doesn't connect, restart your phone and PC.
④ If Windows Firewall asks whether to allow adb, allow it.

④ Go back to Shizuku, tap [Start], then come back to this screen.
